citation: A New Map of Chicago. Chicago Evening Post, April 9, 1869. Reproduced with publication attribution on Chicagology, Ward Map – 2 February 1869.
author: Chicago Evening Post; individual draughtsman unidentified
locator: Historical graphic: https://chicagology.com/wp-content/themes/revolution-20/chicagoimages9/chicagoeveningpostgraphic9apr1869wardmap.jpg . Inspected at 1646 × 2172 pixels. The modern ward table on the same page is excluded.
rights_note: The original graphic is attributed to an 1869 United States newspaper issue, public domain by publication age. Only the historical geographic facts and geometry are derived; the modern host text and table design are not copied as assets.
access_notes: Downloaded and visually inspected the historical graphic on 2026-11-18. The stated newspaper issue has not been independently checked against a second holding. The host’s modern ward table contains contradictory bounds and was not used.
what_it_supplies: Stepped municipal shape: Fullerton east of Western, North Avenue toward the new western limit, the canal southwest edge and Egan Avenue south.
A proposed Jefferson addition north of North Avenue and west of Western, distinguished from present city limits.
what_it_does_not_supply: Surveyed legal-boundary vertices, precise street positions or a reliable population count from the modern host paragraph.
note: Period city-shape evidence, not a legal survey. The approximate local-coordinate boundary is reconstructed. Fortieth/Crawford/Pulaski name equivalence is used for orientation; the modern table is not treated as period evidence.
